name: Apple M2 Ultra
memory_bandwidth_basis: M2 Ultra unified memory ~800 GB/s (1024-bit LPDDR5-6400). Apple-published ~800 GB/s; the full capacity is usable by the GPU - there is no VRAM ceiling because memory is unified.

flops.basis_detail: M2 Ultra GPU ~27.2 TFLOPS FP16 class (76-core GPU variant), republished. Apple does not publish tensor-core-class figures; decode on Apple Silicon is memory-bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound, so this row is secondary to the 800 GB/s bandwidth.

notes: The capacity play for big dense models on used Apple Silicon. 192 GB unified at ~800 GB/s means a 70B Q4 model (~40 GB weights) reads ~40 GB/token -> ~9-11 tok/s est decode (800/40), and it can hold 70B at 8-bit plus long context or Qwen3-235B-A22B. llama.cpp canonical M-series table (discussion #4167): M2 Ultra 94.3 tok/s Q4_0 on a 7B-class model - decode scales almost perfectly with memory bandwidth. Used Mac Studio M2 Ultra 192GB ~$3,200-4,200 (Oct-2026, DRAM-shortage-inflated). Idles ~15-20 W, ~90-150 W under sustained inference, whisper-quiet. Downside: Apple RAM is soldered forever, and used pricing is inflated because new high-RAM Macs are expensive. VENDOR CHECK 2026-10-19: Apple tech specs list 800GB/s memory bandwidth for M2 Ultra with 64GB/128GB/192GB unified memory configurations; 192 GB is the maximum.
